fees.note: Oversize-only single trip permit $30 (IDAPA 39.03.01.107.05.a). If the load is also overweight a single $33 overweight/oversize permit applies instead - only the higher line in this group is charged.
Overweight or overweight/oversize (non-divisible) single trip permit $33 (IDAPA 39.03.01.107.05.b).

Per-mile road use fee, Idaho Code 49-1004(2), set by axle count and gross weight. Column 1 starts at 4 cents/mile and rises 4 cents/mile per 2,000 lb (start: 5 axles 80,001 lb; 6 axles 97,001; 7 axles 114,001; +17,000 lb per extra axle). Column 2 (5 axles from 131,001; 6 from 148,001; 7 from 165,001) starts at $1.02/mile and rises 7 cents/mile per 2,000 lb. Below the column-1 start weight: 4 cents/mile. Not modeled because it depends on axle count.

restrictions.text: Interstate and black-coded routes: loads not over 12' wide, 120' long and 15' high may travel 24 hours/7 days. Larger loads: daylight only (weekends allowed) and no travel after 4 p.m. on the day before a holiday until sunrise the day after (New Year's, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas).
Red-coded routes: daylight only; travel stops 2 p.m. Friday and 2 p.m. the day before a holiday, resumes at dawn Monday / the day after; no weekend or holiday travel.

Over 13' wide: no movement during heavy commuter traffic (6-9 a.m. and 4-6:30 p.m. Mon-Fri) in the Boise valley (I-84 MP 26-59), Coeur d'Alene (I-90 MP 0-17), Idaho Falls (I-15 MP 115-121), Pocatello valley, Twin Falls (US-93 MP 41-53), and within 1 mile of Eagle, Emmett, Garden City, Middleton and Star.

notes: Escort rules come from the ITD pilot/escort map: interstates are white-coded; non_interstate is modeled as black-coded state highways. Red-coded routes are stricter: 8'7"-10' wide = 1 front; 10'1"-12'6" = 1 front + 1 rear; over 75' long = 1 front; over 75' long and over 8'6" wide = 1 front + 1 rear. Check the map for red segments on the route.
The map legend stops at 18' wide; wider/extreme loads get escort requirements on the permit, and a third (advance) pilot may be required to hold opposing traffic (IDAPA 39.03.01.306.13).

Loads over 16' high: the leading pilot car must run a non-metallic height pole; over 16'6" the carrier must contact utilities for power lines. Over-height routes are checked against structure clearances (up to 24 working hours).

Idaho has no formal 'superload' class: flagged thresholds are those needing additional Department approval (IDAPA 39.03.01.305.11) and bridge analysis over 250,000 lb (up to 10 business days; over 800,000 lb third-party analysis). Bridge approval is also needed for any single/steer axle over 35,000 lb.

Legal gross 80,000 lb applies on interstate/national network; Idaho non-interstate state highways allow more by bridge formula and registration (up to 105,500 lb; 129,000 lb on designated routes by permit for divisible loads), so overweight flags on non-interstate miles may be conservative.
Legal overhang: 4' front, 10' rear. Semitrailer 53' on national network routes, 48' elsewhere; 65' overall on routes with severe curvature.
US-12 MP 74-174 (Nez Perce-Clearwater Forest): loads over 16' wide, 150,000 lb or 150' long need US Forest Service review, ISP safety inspection, and may need ambulance/law enforcement escorts.
Permits4idaho is the official ITD permit portal; Special Permit fees are $30 / $33 regardless of distance.
